references.text: God confirms his call to Moses and gives him a sign that he has sent him
God repeats his promise to send Moses and teach him what to say
God commands Moses again to go to Pharaoh and demand that the Israelites be allowed to leave
Moses is commanded to speak to Pharaoh about letting the children of Israel leave the land
The psalm describes how God sent his servant Moses to Egypt
Micah reminds the people that God brought them out of Egypt and sent Moses
Joshua reminds the people that God sent Moses and Aaron and led their fathers out of Egypt
Samuel reminds the people that the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, who led their fathers out of Egypt
Isaiah describes how God brought the people up from the sea with Moses as shepherd
Stephen quotes God's call to Moses and describes how God sent him as leader and deliverer
The letter to the Hebrews mentions Moses' faith when he left Egypt and did not fear the king's anger
Connection between the mission of exodus and its fulfillment through God's judgments.
Transition from Moses' mission to God's own action to free the people.
The deliverance of the people from Egypt as the foundation for God's new covenant.
Confirmation that the mission to lead the people out has been entrusted to both brothers.
The NT's retelling of the call at the burning bush as confirmation of God's plan of salvation.
The derivation as a means to reveal the Lord's identity to the nations.
A repeated command emphasizing God's unyielding demand for liberation.
